what: the trained addition network of experiments/addition (a + b for a, b in 0..99 as 100 opaque tokens -> three digit tokens), its final parameters, for the in-post widget (src/viz/addnet.js)
format: raw little-endian IEEE float16, row-major, the tensors in `order` back to back; `offset` and `size` count float16 elements, `byte_offset` bytes
forward: x = concat(E[a], E[b]); h1 = relu(x @ W1 + b1); h2 = relu(h1 @ W2 + b2); logits = (h2 @ W3 + b3) as 3 rows of 10; digit i = argmax(row i); digits are hundreds, tens, units

accuracy.note: recomputed from this float16 file in float64 arithmetic over all 10,000 pairs by export_weights.py; the argmax digits equal those of the float32 weights on every pair, and those of the float64 training run on the test set (train.py's float32_check: test_exact 1.00000)

provenance.script: experiments/addition/train.py (the standalone addition repository has the canonical copy) with --save-weights and --checkpoints, then export_weights.py beside it
provenance.retrain_check: seed 0 trained again on another Apple Silicon Mac (Python 3.9.6, numpy 2.0.2 with Accelerate, the recorded run's versions) with the default flags plus the weight-saving flags: all 491 logged rows of weights/results-seed0-weights.json are identical in every field to the recorded run (results.json; the blog's public/data/addition.json); meta differs only in date and runtime (937 s)
provenance.conversion: float32 (as saved by train.py) cast to float16 by numpy astype; 12504 of 152094 values lie below float16's normal range and 11469 were flushed to zero
